principles: One canonical REVIEW contract eliminates drift across all five reviewer lanes.
Agent guidance projects System semantics but never replaces mechanical gate facts.
Dynamic Finding authority remains unchanged and retired vocabulary is not active Task Context authority.
Scope follows applicability and gate impact rather than severity alone.
Tests must prove delivery, isolation, and pre-digest rejection of contradictory Task Context.
drivers: Five REVIEW lanes and two envelope paths need byte-consistent behavior.
Open-source English quality and canonical Proof-or-Stop identities are required.
Signed reviewers proved that generic migration exceptions allow authority laundering.
The user requested Agent behavior while preserving Dynamic Finding System consistency.

options.name: Central resolver injection with strict Task Context guard
Duplicate rules in each reviewer template
cons: Does not solve Task Context authority injection

options.name: Implement Dynamic Finding runtime now
cons: Requires schema, handler, predicate, registry, migration, and gate work

chosen: Central resolver injection with strict Task Context guard
rationale: Inject one canonical contract only for the five REVIEW lanes after base-body selection, keep the authoritative Dynamic Finding plan unchanged, reject active retired or contradictory authority in Story/checklist/verificationIntent Task Context before digesting, and verify both envelope modes plus non-REVIEW isolation.

preMortem.trigger: Injection uses a broad modular-role predicate
preMortem.consequence: Owner or implementer receives unauthorized reviewer behavior
preMortem.mitigation: Exhaustively assert every active non-REVIEW role omits the contract in both modes.

preMortem.trigger: A malicious positive statement is wrapped in test or migration prose
preMortem.consequence: A signed reviewer envelope carries stale semantics
preMortem.mitigation: Scan affirmative residue even inside quoted-fixture or mutation prose and add exact RED/GREEN bypass cases.

preMortem.scenario: Prompt prose is mistaken for gate evidence
preMortem.trigger: requiredCheckIds or rendered text is consumed as lifecycle proof
preMortem.consequence: Review passes without signed reviewer evidence
preMortem.mitigation: Keep prompt metadata non-evidentiary and verify no authority dataflow into gate consumers.

preMortem.scenario: Identity migration leaves obsolete verifier pins
preMortem.trigger: Frozen PLAN commands reference retired role IDs, paths, or version
preMortem.mitigation: Use controlled replan to canonicalize all verifier pins and require 60 mechanical receipts.

preMortem.trigger: Pins are updated before negative tests
preMortem.consequence: Baseline passes while behavior is unsafe
preMortem.mitigation: Run focused RED/GREEN mutation checks before reviewed baseline updates.
